name: Siaqodb
tagline: Embedded object and document database for .NET, Xamarin and Unity with LINQ queries; now inactive.
description: Siaqodb was an embedded NoSQL object database for .NET from CCSTM Computing, aimed at desktop, mobile and game developers. It stored POCO object graphs either object by object or as whole documents, queried them through a full LINQ provider, supported partial and eager loading, async APIs and pluggable encryption, and in its last versions used LMDB as an ACID storage engine. It ran on .NET, Mono/MonoMac, UWP, Xamarin.iOS, Xamarin.Android and Unity3D, and a sync add-on replicated client data to CouchDB, MongoDB or Azure Table storage. After the company stopped trading the source was published on GitHub under MIT in 2020-2021, with a final NuGet release (5.5.0.12) in March 2021; nothing has happened since.
statusNote: Vendor ceased operations; source released under MIT in 2021 with no activity since. For embedded .NET storage use LiteDB, Realm or SQLite.

pricing.notes: Formerly a commercial product; now free MIT-licensed source with no support.

strengths: Stores plain .NET object graphs with no mapping layer
Full LINQ provider and async API
Ran across desktop, Xamarin mobile and Unity games
Optional sync to CouchDB, MongoDB or Azure storage
weaknesses: Unmaintained since 2021; targets the Xamarin era rather than modern .NET MAUI
Small user base and sparse documentation
useCases: Maintaining older Xamarin or Unity apps built on Siaqodb
